mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate investment and consumption, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not higher than baseline during low FEDFUNDS periods.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment rate signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Returns remain positive despite rising unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth and increased housing starts indicate robust demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are negative despite strong GDP and housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing industrial production growth signals supply constraints, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are positive despite slowing industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing employment suggests economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: Returns are negative despite employment growth.

mechanism_narrative: Declining retail sales indicate weaker demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are positive despite declining retail sales.

mechanism_narrative: Low FEDFUNDS and high UNRATE indicate economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are positive despite low FEDFUNDS and high unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts in a recession may not prevent negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Returns are positive despite rising housing starts in a recession.
